claims.text: The AlCrFeNiSi feedstock is spherical, high quality, and has a uniform particle-size distribution and standard as-atomized morphology.
Machine-learning-guided optimization can be used to select laser powder bed fusion process conditions.
An ML-optimized low-energy-density scanning strategy is applicable to AlCrFeNiSi.
Reducing laser power by 10–20%, while adapting scan speed and beam path, will moderate heat input.
Moderate substrate preheating at approximately 200°C may help moderate the relevant thermal conditions.
The proposed process can achieve greater than 98% relative density in AlCrFeNiSi.
The intervention is applicable to miniature geometries having features of approximately 1–5 mm.
The AlCrFeNiSi components can be processed under ambient atmosphere using the proposed L-PBF regime.
Reduced thermal input will moderate thermal gradients.
Moderated thermal gradients will diminish residual stress in the manufactured components.
Reduced thermal input will produce a more homogeneous, finer-grained microstructure with fewer thermal defects.
Conventional high-thermal-load L-PBF produces high local peak temperatures, steep thermal gradients, and rapid thermal cycling.
Rapid thermal cycling in conventional high-thermal-load processing causes residual stress and microstructural degradation.
Controlling peak temperatures and thermal gradients will improve mechanical properties.
The intervention will decrease processing complexity relative to tightly managed high-heat-input processing.
Relative to conventional high-energy L-PBF, the intervention will significantly reduce residual stress.
Relative to conventional high-energy L-PBF, the intervention will increase yield strength and ductility.
Relative to conventional high-energy L-PBF, the intervention will produce a more uniform, defect-minimized microstructure.
The cited XGBoost approach was experimentally validated using 316L stainless steel, AlSi10Mg, and Fe60Co15Ni15Cr10 powders and targeted relative density greater than 98%.
Failure to obtain statistically significant residual-stress reductions and corresponding mechanical-property improvements relative to the conventional-process control would falsify the hypothesis.
